Even though he showed a smile, Noah's figure, wreathed in angrily scorching crimson-gold flames, still couldn't help but tremble with constant rhythmic shaking.
The tremors were a physical manifestation of the war being fought in every cell of his body.
Noah felt the eyes of Alexander remain on him with steady focus.
They were the eyes of someone younger looking up to someone older, as if they found his actions unfathomably grand.
As if his suffering was a monument to be admired rather than a torture to be pitied.
He shook his head excruciatingly at this perception.
The scorching blurry prompts continued to flow over his eyes every now and then, a ticker tape of his own torture converted to power.
+100 Sextillion Complexity and Purity gained from an unsurpassable
effort...
They were unfathomably immense gains that came from this excruciating effort, numbers that would have taken days and weeks for him to accumulate through normal means.
Noah felt it all washing over him.
He tried to focus his scattered
attention on his other self, on Ozymandias, who should be wrapping up a battle soon.
Because THE Immolation Of The Sacrilegious Savage was a curse as much as a weapon.
He was barely handling it with all his accumulated will.
Other existences, for them it was utterly disastrous if he actively
allowed the contagion to spread!
Far in the distance, the battle raged with renewed intensity.
But it was
a massacre of a different kind.
Ozymandias stood amidst the violet storm of the Emotive Legion like
a dark star.
His humanoid body, wreathed in the same crimson-gold fire that burned Noah, erupted with terrible purpose.
Thousands of tentacles, slick with obsidian-crimson hunger and blazing with the contagious agony of the Immolation, shot out in every direction like seeking missiles.
They rushed towards the Civilizational Legions of Emotives with predatory intent.
The moment they made contact, the effect was instantaneous and devastating.
The Emotives, beings of pure concentrated feeling, were instantly wreathed in THE Immolation Of The Sacrilegious Savage.
Most of them felt the excruciating pain for a second or two.
That was all their sanity could withstand before it shattered like glass.
Their minds broke.
Their wills evaporated.
They did not fight back and they did not try to flee.
They simply... collapsed their own existence voluntarily as Ozymandias would then devour them!
It was a wave of mass suicide, triggered by a pain that no being should
ever have to feel.
Others scattered in absolute terror, their formations breaking apart as
they fled from the burning touch of Ozymandias's tentacles like prey
fleeing a predator.
Because of this devastating effect, the Legion of Emotives became scattered and broken down.
The Civilizational Legion of Law and Deborah, watching from their defensive line, stared in stupor and disbelief.
They had been fighting a losing battle for what felt like eons,
and now in mere moments their enemy was dissolving before their
eyes.
As for Ozymandias himself, his existence felt the same excruciating pain as Noah.
Every movement was torture.
Every extension of a tentacle was a scream trapped in his throat threatening to escape.
But he endured!
And for his endurance while moving even more aggressively, Harvest continued to descend on him in waves.
He gained 100 Sextillion Complexity and Purity every so often, his power skyrocketing as he turned his own suffering into a weapon of mass destruction.
This battle could effectively be considered over and done.
As much as
Noah was being afflicted with a terrifying curse from a Primordial Sovereign, he had gotten his hands on a truly terrifying weapon.
Pain, it turned out, was the ultimate offensive capability.
Noah watched this unfold through the haze of his own agony, and despite everything he felt something like satisfaction.
The Emotives were breaking not because they were weak but because the pain was simply beyond any reasonable capacity to endure.
Even beings of 300 Sextillion Complexity were folding within seconds.
And he was standing here, minutes into the Brand, still conscious and
still fighting.
What does that make me?
The thought came unbidden and he almost wanted to laugh again.
Alexander spoke again, his voice cutting through Noah's internal
thoughts "Is there any principle or authority that might alleviate... this?"
Noah shook his head slowly, each movement sending fresh lances of agony through his neck.
"This is an attack from THE Living Elemental himself.
No one here has the authority to counter it.
Unless you have
the distinction of THE."
"Then what do we do?"
What could one do indeed.
At this though, Noah remembered his own words.
Unless you have the distinction of THE.
Who...did he know with a distinction of THE?
His eyes pulsed with tyranny!
His vision swam and refocused.
The prompts kept coming.
+150 Sextillion Complexity and Purity gained from an unsurpassable effort...
The numbers were climbing faster now.
His existence was learning to harvest from the pain more efficiently, extracting power from suffering with ruthless precision.
It was the third view of pain made manifest.
Pain as a condition of
reality.
Pain as background radiation.
Pain as the price of ascension.
He had paid the price before in smaller denominations.
Now he was
paying in bulk, and existence was forced to acknowledge the transaction.
In the distance, Ozymandias's tentacles swept through another
cluster of Emotives.
They scattered like leaves before a storm, and those too slow to escape dissolved hunger in his jaws with expressions of relief on their fading faces.
Khor appeared near Ozymandias, her small form blazing with hunger
as she coordinated the assault.
Riya and others cautiously floated
above.
The crimson-gold flames continued to burn as the pain continued to scream, and Noah continued to stand strong!

chapters.title: Chapter 4497 At The Darkest Hour II
paragraphs: In the Infiniverse.

As Noah burned with immense pain that transcended comprehension, Elyndra stood before him with shaking eyes. She could see it clearly, the excruciating agony he was going through written in every tremor of his form, in every flicker of the crimson-gold flames that wrapped around him like chains of suffering.
But Noah kept his calmness even as his body shook. His voice was steady despite the cost it took to speak.

"I won't be able to continue infusing you with Perpetual Harvest so..." Before he could finish, the space beside them rippled with authority. The humanoid figure of The Infiniverse appeared with deliberate precision. She stood tall and ethereal, her form composed of countless spinning Omniverses and flowing rivers of verdant-gold light. But her eyes, those infinite pools that normally held warmth for her Master, were particularly cold.
One could see that she was enraged and simply containing everything with titanic effort, holding back a fury that could unmake Folds!
Noah nodded to her with understanding passing between them, and then he disappeared from this domain entirely.
He left The Infiniverse, who had full access to Perpetual Harvest, to continue the infusion with Elyndra in his place.

As this scene played out, something extraordinary began to happen. Existence itself began to buzz with strange resonance. Drums, deep and solemn, began to bloom from nowhere and everywhere at once. Pianonic sounds followed, ethereal and haunting, creating a melody that seemed to emerge from the fabric of reality itself. Then voices, wordless and beautiful, echoed out across this space. Across Existence.
When the stolen flame descends
When the ancient powers demand their toll
Does the fire cleanse or break
Does it forge or consume whole?
It was as if Existence itself was buzzing with a melody for this momentous occasion, acknowledging what was transpiring.

The Infiniverse unfurled her hands with mechanical precision and began to release verdant-gold brilliance into Elyndra. The light was beautiful and terrible, carrying the weight of Perpetual Harvest within its threads.
But The Infiniverse seemingly didn't care much for the task at hand. Her focus was elsewhere, her rage barely contained.
Elyndra looked at her with concern. "Is he going to be okay? What did that to him?"

The Infiniverse remained cold and silent for a long moment, as if this stillness was the only thing she could do to keep back the tsunami of rage. When she finally spoke, her voice dripped with loathing and carried an immensity that made the surrounding space tremble.
"THE Living Elemental."
The drums grew heavier in the background, the piano more insistent.

The Infiniverse's eyes blazed with barely contained fury as she continued, her words a solemn vow wrapped in absolute certainty. "The pathetic flicker of primordial authority that thought it could mark my Master and walk away unscathed. The entity that believed its age and power made it untouchable."
Her voice dropped to something far more dangerous, a whisper that carried the weight of inevitability.
"I will personally grind THE Living Elemental down to existential dust. I will erase every particle of its authority. I will unmake its very
concept until not even the memory of its existence remains to pollute reality. This I swear on the foundations of my being."
This is the Brand of sacred violation
The price of touching what was never his
Crimson-gold immolation
Where mortal will meets the abyss
The chorus swelled!
Existence continued a grand symphony!
Elsewhere, panning out across various regions of The Infiniverse.
In an isolated domain of The Abode of The Early Creature, Riya stood motionless. She wore simple blue bloomers and a blue tank top.
She watched with those teary eyes as Noah, excruciatingly burning in crimson-gold flames, turned to leave the domain.
The pain in his movements was visible.
But he was leaving to protect her from what he had become.
The shield steps before the sword
The leader takes the blow
While armies scatter, terrified
Of pain they'll never know

In a different isolated domain, this one decorated with obsidian furniture and dark elegance, Barbatos stood trembling. She wore an obsidian sundress that flowed like liquid shadow, and her normally composed demeanor had shattered completely. She shook with rage and sorrow mixed together in equal measure as another one of Noah's bodies, equally wreathed in flames and equally trembling, also prepared to leave her presence.
"Don't," she whispered, "Please don't."
But Noah could not stay. The risk was too great. The contagion too
dangerous.
He left without responding.
Seconds break the strongest minds
Minutes shatter souls
But time keeps passing, relentless
As the burning takes its toll

In yet another isolated domain, this one filled with gently falling snow that never seemed to accumulate, Adelaide stood in a flowing blue dress. The snowflakes caught in her hair like diamonds, but her eyes held only sorrow as she looked toward Noah's burning form.
"Let me..." she started. "Let me feel what you feel. Let me feel the same
pain." Noah shook his head with agonizing slowness, each movement sending fresh waves of torture through his frame. For the sake of his loved ones, he could not even be near them at this moment!

He wasn't afraid of them accidentally coming in contact with him and being branded with the same curse. What he couldn't bear was being around when one of them inevitably came close or felt like they wanted to share that burden.

It was causing him this many issues already. He would not be able to watch his own people suffer THE Immolation of the Sacrilegious Savage as they eventually collapsed their own existence just to escape the pain!
So he simply shook his head lightly, and even from Adelaide, he left. The symphony continued to play from Existence itself, solemn and
heavy.
What is pain but a teacher?
What is agony but proof?
That something still exists to feel That there's still a will to move
The scene shifted again to show something unprecedented.
All of Noah's bodies throughout The Infiniverse, every single iteration
that had been spread across countless domains and separated to
prevent the spread of the Brand, began to gather in a single isolated
area.
This space was filled with sandy golden dream authority that swirled like desert winds frozen in time.
And then, with excruciating slowness, they began fusing into each
other.
He compressed himself back into singularity, consolidating his
existence despite the torture it caused.
Until finally, only a single Noah floated in that golden space, trembling
but whole. The humanoid form of The Infiniverse appeared before her Master
with silent grace. She looked at his trembling form with eyes that held infinite sorrow and infinite determination. "Can Master follow me?" she asked quietly.
Noah looked at her briefly and nodded once.
The two of them warped through space with The Infiniverse guiding
them, and they appeared above a radiant blue world that pulsed with concentrated authority.
The moment Noah saw it, his eyes buzzed.
This was the Cultivation Citadel!
The feature The Infiniverse had designed where one would be
imposed with the weight of existence many times over, where if they
adapted they would gain an explosive increase in Complexity and
Purity.
But even moving for Noah was painful at this moment. If he added an elevated weight of existence on top of what he was already bearing...
Here the answer to pain manifests
In trembling, burning form Pain becomes a currency And endurance, the new norm
The Infiniverse looked at her Master with an expression that mixed
love and necessity and terrible resolve.

"I've been elevating it as we increase in power," she said softly. "The Cultivation Citadel is even grander and harder than before. I know it will be excruciating for Master. I know it seems like you cannot adapt
to this pain."
She paused.
"But... I need you to go in, Master."
Noah's body shook with a solemn tyranny.
He looked at the Cultivation Citadel that would make his pain
hundreds of times worse, and he truly did not want to enter it. But this was a calamity as much as an opportunity. He needed to
make use of it. He needed to do something to adapt to it even if adaptation seemed impossible.
So even though he did not want to, even though every fiber of his being screamed in protest...
Noah flew toward the Cultivation Citadel.
His body, wreathed in the curse of THE Living Elemental, descended
like a falling star wrapped in chains of agony.
Lesser beings would have long since perished from what he faced!
But he persevered!
In the space above, The Infiniverse watched silently as her Master
descended. Beside her, RUIN/EDEN materialized with an expression that was pained and heavy.
"We could have waited," RUIN/EDEN said quietly. "For him to adapt a bit more, to see if the pain gets any less..."
And yet, The Infiniverse shook her head decisively.
"It will not get less. It will not get any less." The surrounding existence continued the solemn symphony as another chorus swelled across reality.
This is the Brand of sacred violation
The mark that even Sovereigns cannot erase Crimson-gold immolation
Burns across time and space
RUIN/EDEN listened silently, and then her expression shifted to
something enraged and terrible.
"THE Living Elemental..." she started.
But The Infiniverse's focus was entirely on the scene below. Her eyes
reflected her Master's burning figure as he reached the earth of the Cultivation Citadel and tried to stand with excruciating effort.
His knees buckled as his hands pressed against the ground. Every
muscle trembled.
But he stood.
As she watched this impossible display of will, golden lines of
terrifying wonder began to leak from The Infiniverse's infinite eyes as she had never seen her Master like this!
They fell like molten stars, each one carrying the weight of her fury and her pride and her absolute devotion.

"I am going to rip THE Living Elemental apart," she whispered, but her voice carried across dimensions. "Atom by atom. Particle of authority by particle of authority. I will dissect every weaving of its existence. I

will make it experience pain beyond what it inflicted. I will make it beg for the mercy of non-existence. I will make it wish it had never experienced existence at all. And then, when it has suffered for eons...
I will grant it oblivion and erase even that mercy from the memory of
reality."
The symphony and chorus resounded even heavier now, the voices of
existence itself acknowledging the vow.
Let THE Ancients tremble
At what their curse became
Not a weapon of destruction
But a forge for his ascension's flame HUUM!
On this day, The Infiniverse shed a tear.
On this day, the entirety of The Infiniverse, the countless Frequencies
of Existence, the Wheels of Existence, the Omniverses, the Domains
of Existence, all of it trembled in resonance with her emotion. And oh, for the entity that caused The Infiniverse to shed a tear...
bless their poor souls.
The Infiniverse turned to RUIN/EDEN, and when she spoke her voice

was cold and tyrannical and absolute. "Mobilize the Primus Inevitabilities into all Elemental Folds immediately," she commanded with the force of inevitability itself. "Convert every single Elemental into The Way of Mana, whether by choice or by force. I do not care which. Erase every single signature of The Primordial Civilization of Elementals outside THE Loom. Convert
every single iota into The Derivative Primordial Civilization of
Elemental under the banner of Mana."
Her eyes blazed brighter.

"Afterwards we will begin devouring and incorporating all Transcendent and Minor Elemental Folds without exception. After that... I shall begin devouring every single remnant of the Shattered First Folds, all the Transcendent Folds and Minor Folds across Observable Existence. I shall take it all. Every piece. Every fragment."
Her voice dropped to something even more dangerous.
"They want to play? Let us fucking play."
The command was heavy and absolute. RUIN/EDEN nodded silently,
her own expression grim with determination, and then she
disappeared to carry out the orders.
The flames don't cease their hunger
The pain knows no reprieve But standing in the inferno
Is the choice that sets him free
The final chorus and symphony swelled across existence as The
Infiniverse stood alone above the Cultivation Citadel. She overlooked Noah, her Master, at seemingly his most pained state.
She would watch over him. She would guard him. She would feel
everything he felt.
After all, they were connected in a Quintessential and irreversible
manner.
If she wanted to, she could feel what he felt through their bond. And this whole time, from the moment THE Living Elemental had
branded him, she had subjected herself to feel the inescapable pain her Master endured!
She trembled alongside him and she suffered alongside him.
And she would have her vengeance for it.
Below, Noah took his first step into the deeper gravity of the Cultivation Citadel, and the weight increased tenfold. And The Infiniverse watched with golden lines still falling from her
eyes, each one a declaration of war against those who had dared to harm what was hers like this!

The weight of existence pressed down on him like the gravity of a collapsing star. The crimson-gold flames continued their endless feast on his being.

possessed the distinction of THE.

THE Dead Order!

He closed his eyes with agonizing slowness. In the next moment, he focused his weavings of existence toward that unique space that held The Veil which divided him and Sigrid from THE Dead Order on the other side.
The domain that didn't really exist anywhere in physical Observable Existence, but in a unique conceptual space where Sigrid was siphoning The Civilizational Authority of Order.
At this moment, the scene shifted to that ethereal realm.
In that space between spaces, Noah had already made distance and moved away from Sigrid who was looking at him with pained eyes.
Even here, even in this conceptual domain, his figure was burning with crimson-gold fire that refused to be extinguished.
On the other side of The Veil, THE Dead Order sat upon her throne of
white marble and looked at him with a particularly unfavorable expression.

In the last few hours, with Sigrid becoming more and more powerful naturally, her rate of siphoning Order had become even more immense. The flow of Civilizational Authority being drained through The Veil had increased to torrential levels.
So THE Dead Order was not their biggest fan at this moment.
But even she tilted her head with curiosity and looked at those flames burning around his figure with something like astonishment in her ancient eyes.
"What did you do?" she asked.
Noah looked at her through The Veil with eyes that burned despite the pain, his voice steady despite the cost of speaking.
"Are you familiar with the curses of entities with THE distinction?"
She replied with incredulity that he could even ask such a question. "You can say that."

He nodded slowly and continued with that same terrible calmness. "I seem to have pissed off THE Living Elemental, and that pathetic excuse for a fire has proceeded to brand me with THE Immolation Of The Sacrilegious Savage. A constant excruciating burning that cares not for Complexity or Purity. An indefinite burning until I collapse my own existence."

As he said this with such casual matter-of-factness, THE Dead Order looked at him with sheer incredulity written across her features. "How are you not dead?" she demanded. "How have you not collapsed your existence already?"
Noah looked at her calmly through the excruciating pain, his gaze unwavering.

"The two of us are some of the few powers that exist outside of THE Loom. We both wish to survive The Fallout and come through on the other side stronger than before." His voice carried the weight of inevitability. "An answer to The Fallout lies with existences that have the distinction of THE. You have such a distinction, even if you do not have the full power of THE currently."
He paused, letting his words sink in.

"If you and I were able to come to an understanding... maybe The Fallout would be something that we can easily get past. This is what I have always thought. Right now, faced with this ordeal, would you happen to have an answer or solution or knowledge regarding how such a curse could be taken care of?"
His eyes gleamed with something dangerous.
"And to show my goodwill..."

Noah nodded toward Sigrid, and in the next moment the massive river of white Order that was flowing from the other side of The Veil to Sigrid stopped abruptly. It rapidly reduced and became a barely imperceptible line as barely any Civilizational Authority of Order was being siphoned anymore.

THE Dead Order looked at such a scene with somber eyes, looking at Noah as if he were a dead man walking as she asked with genuine curiosity, "What exactly did you do to make THE Living Elemental so enraged that he would exert his authority outside of THE Loom? With the suppression of Existence itself laid down by THE Creature, any entity with THE distinction would pay a heavy cost to unleash even a semblance of their power like this outside THE Loom. Just what did you do?"
Noah did not answer such a question.
He simply floated closer to The Veil with deliberate movements, appearing inches away from it, close enough that the flames around
him cast dancing shadows across her throne.
He asked again with calm tyranny amidst all the burning, "Do you have
a solution?"
At such a direct question, THE Dead Order became utterly still as if she were thinking carefully about her options.

Noah looked at her with eyes that seemed to pierce through layers of existence, and as if he could seemingly see inside of her being and what decision she was about to make, he said with quiet certainty, "In your head right now, you are debating two choices. I do advise for you to lean towards the better choice for your sake and mine."
At such presumptuous words, THE Dead Order smiled with a sense of
brutality and calculation. She leaned back on her throne and laughed with genuine amusement.
"Since you already seem to know then I will choose the other choice,"

she said with cruel delight. "Why would I help you? You are an antagonist against what I wish to achieve. And now that you have been struck with such an affliction, your existence will likely collapse itself soon enough, even though it should have done so some time ago."
Her smile widened.

"After you are collapsed... this little vile Young Order you have been defiling, who is so emotionally connected to you that she is holding back tears right now as you burn... she would lose her protector. Any semblance of Civilization that you are building will crumble. And once the one protecting her has crumbled, I can send my Guides of Order to the other side of The Veil without worry and claim that vile Young Order beside you. I will erase her existence completely and fuse with
what she has."
HUUM!
She spread her hands as if presenting an obvious truth.
across her form like wildfire!
THE Dead Order opened her eyes with absolute incredulity and
shock, her mind unable to process what had just occurred. Noah used that instant moment of shock to rapidly shoot back across
to the other side of The Veil with desperate speed!
THE Dead Order then howled out in rage as the flames climbed
higher up her body!
Immense waves of Order erupted from her like a tsunami, blanketing
down on the flames that had already covered half of her lower body!
"YOU CAN CROSS THE VEIL?!" she roared with disbelief and fury mixing together. "You sycophantic fuck!"

Noah looked at her from the safety of the other side with an utterly cold and tyrannical gaze that held no sympathy whatsoever. "Watch your language, O pristine and righteous Order," he said with quiet venom. "I told you to make a different choice. You did not. So
now... we share the same affliction."
His eyes blazed with satisfaction despite the pain.
"I sincerely hope that you have a solution for it."
BOOM!
Rageful waves of Order erupted like volcanic fury as shockingly, Noah
observed seas of white authority trying desperately to press down on
the flames that were rising to cover the massive body of THE Dead
Order. They were shockingly slowing the advance of the flames from covering her entirely, the Civilizational Authority of Order combating the curse with desperate intensity.
Noah could feel the eyes of THE Dead Order vibrating with immense
pain and incredulity mixing with absolute rage, and her domineering voice bellowed out in the next moment with a single word that shook
the entire domain.
"OSMONT!!!"
The roar was primal and furious and filled with a pain she had not
experienced in eons.
Noah simply watched with cold satisfaction as THE Dead Order experienced the same burning he had been enduring, and he waited to see what choice she would make now!

chapters.title: Chapter 4499: At The Darkest Hour IV
paragraphs: As the rage ofTHE Dead Orderbecame apparent and built to a crescendo, she seemed like she was about to unleash even more words filled with venom and malice... and yet the rising flames ofTHE Immolation Of The Sacrilegious Savagecaused her to be unable to even do this as she had to focus entirely on survival.
She glared towards Noah with eyes that promised retribution as seas of her authority continued to crash down on the flames with desperate intensity.

Noah looked towards Sigrid to confirm something important, and he saw that she had already completely stopped siphoning off the Civilizational Authority of Order. Just in case this would transfer the curse ofTHE Living Elementalto her as well.
Noah looked atTHE Dead Orderonce more through The Veil with calm tyranny.
"So, I ask you again," he said with measured words. "Do you have a solution to such a curse? You should be able to feel it intimately now."
As he said this, he also saw the prompts that flashed before his eyes with brilliant light.
|You have carried out a bold action of unsurpassable effort and audacity.|
|Your choices currently cause an existence much more complex than you to feel unbearable pain.|
|By spreading THE Immolation Of The Sacrilegious Savage to THE Dead Order, you have created a situation of unprecedented consequence.|
|Depending on the result of your actions, you can potentially harvest unfathomable wonders.|
He simply watched these prompts come and go like waves as he looked at THE Dead Order who gazed at him with eyes of utter malice and suffering combined.
She struggled against the flames for a long moment before speaking through gritted teeth, her voice dripping with hatred.

"Only THE Civilizational Authority can go against THE Civilizational Authority," she said with cruel finality. "You are not at that level. You are far from that level, and as of now, you will never reach that level. You could go past Septillions, Octillions, Nonillions, and even Decillions in Complexity and Purity, and you, Osmont...would not reach THE."
Her expression twisted with spiteful satisfaction despite her pain.

"All the efforts you have made, the grand Civilization you have been trying to build... all of it will crumble even before The Fallout happens. And I will be waiting for that patiently, Osmont. I will be waiting for your complete cession and collapse that you will carry out with your own hands when the pain you feel becomes unbearable."
Her voice rose to something like triumph through the agony.
"Rejoice, Osmont! Rejoice, for your death is coming!"

Her expression turned utterly spiteful and hateful towards the end, and after she finished these words she waved her hands with tremendous effort. A white veil emerged to surround her completely, blocking off any view of her brilliance and figure as if she did not even wish to look at him while she fought against the encroachingTHE Immolation Of The Sacrilegious Savage.
Noah looked at the scene in silence as behind him the figure of Sigrid asked with desperation in her voice, "What can I do?"
And the answer to this as Noah continued to burn was a calm and simple, "Nothing. It’s okay."
His eyes burned brightly as he thought of her answer echoing in his mind.Only THE Civilizational Authority can go against THE Civilizational Authority.
He closed his eyes and the scene of this ethereal domain, of the space between spaces, faded away as his focus came once more to his body that was within the Cultivation Citadel.
He strained as his legs and arms trembled with effort, and he only managed to stand upright while bearing the flames through sheer tyrannical will.
In the next moment, the figure of The Infiniverse made her descent, and she actually came bearing gifts in her hands.
She voiced out with shining eyes, "Elyndra provided these gifts from The First Farmer. As the first course of action for his Civilization, he planted seeds of effort that boreThe Fruits of Effort."
She held them forward reverently.

"Consuming such a fruit will grant one the harvest of effort that they have been putting in across existence from the day they were born. The screaming the moment you arrived into the world in that hospital. As your mother cried in happiness and clutched you and held you. As your heart beat furiously and as your lungs sought air. As your teeth formed and grew, as your body and organs continued to develop. As you went through schools in the effort of communicating with others. As your first love turned you down because you were not enough. As you went through an apocalypse and lost your mother. As you awakened and made the effort to cast your very first fireball. All the effort since the day you were born..."
As she said this with a sense of hope, she threw these Fruits of Effort to him.
Noah managed to grab them with trembling hands, his steady gaze filled with tyranny looking at them as he nodded with understanding.
"Give my thanks to The First Farmer," Noah said with genuine gratitude despite the pain.
Thereafter, he opened his mouth unnaturally wide and swallowed the entirety of the first Fruit of Effort in a single gulp before he proceeded to do the same with the others in rapid succession.
Effort.
It took a great deal of effort to be who he was since the day that he was born.
Noah felt the vibrant Fruits of Effort bloom across his existence as everything began to shake and tremble with accumulated power.

His existence was currently surrounded by an array of harvests all around him, with the harvests of encroaching upon The Primordial Civilization of Elemental being immense and still being gathered. His Architect’s Bulwarks would undoubtedly advance and reach a glorious stage of achievement from all of this harvest.
And right now, as he sensed the Fruits of Effort dissolving into his existence, his eyes began to flicker with memories as he sensed the very first breath that he took the day that he was born.
As he began to feel all that effort accumulating, he spoke with commanding authority.

"All the effort of my existence from the day that I was born, from when I was even in my mother’s womb... let all of that effort flow into persevering and surviving and coming up with a solution forTHE Immolation Of The Sacrilegious Savage."
All the effort of his existence even before he was born!

His existence began to buzz with accumulated power as even while scorching flames tore apart every single cell in every atom... even as his existence continued to be battered by a pain that other existences could not handle for a second...
HUUUM!
His existence began to vibrate and resonate as verdant-gold light permeated all around him in waves of increasing intensity.
|All your Principles surge with unprecedented brilliance.|
|Retroactive Harvestingof Perpetual Harvest has been activated.|
|Harvest of Intenthas been activated.|
|The Laborer’s Paradisemultiplies all efforts at this moment by 1,000 times.|
|Primus Singularityhas been activated.|
|Hardship Dissolutionof The Principle of Arcana Infinitum has been activated.|
|The Cheating Architect has called uponThe Developmental Consoleof your existence.|
|The ultimate feature ofExistential Mod Supporthas been triggered.|
|Existential Mod Supportcan manifest concepts or weavings not currently present in Observable Existence.|
|You are attempting to birth something new.|
Noah read through all of these prompts as they all burned with an unfathomable amount of effort and utter pristine glory.
He felt all of his five Principles burn with a light that almost exceeded the crimson-gold flames that were excruciatingly burning him
Almost.
And as all of this effort gathered and concentrated, as every ounce of effort from even before he was born burned for this singular moment in time...
The one thing that remained constant within him burned furiously the most.
His blue-gold Mana. His Primus Mana.
How infinitely grand they were was its own infinite effort.
|Mana is behind countless weavings of existence itself.|
|Mana is behind pain.|
|Mana is behind change.|
|Mana is behind mutations.|
|Mana is behind evolution.|
|Mana is behind adaptation.|
|Fundamental Truth: Mana dictates that if an answer does not exist in Observable Existence, Mana can simply be the source that brings a new answer to fruition.|
|Existential Mod Support agrees with this assessment.|
|A Glorious Mutation is underway.|
|A Glorious Evolution is underway.|
|THE Civilizational Authority Resistance has begun to bloom within your existence. THE Organ of Civilization seeks to bloom within your existence.|
BOOOM!

paragraphs: THE Civilizational Authority Resistance.
THE Organ of Civilization.

Noah heard these words booming across his existence while he felt the immense amplified Effort across his being, from the moment he was born and even before, all flowing towards this singular purpose.
What was this?

He analyzed the concept with cold logic even as his existence burned. He was too far away fromTHE. Even though Complexity and Purity could not be considered the immense factors in attainingTHE, even though right now he was in the Septillions, he instinctively knew that he was truly far away from the next Scale of Existence.
So for him to be awakening anything that had capitalTHEin the name was utterly astounding.
And the only way that it made sense was through the simple words that echoed in his mind.
Only THE Civilizational Authority can go against THE Civilizational Authority.

The Glorious Evolution that all of his accumulated effort was seeking to impose could only have something withTHEin it or it would have been ineffective against the curse. The logic was sound. Existence itself was confirming it.
So at this moment, as Noah felt the excruciating pain of burning across the entirety of his existence, he observed as the immense amplified effort of his entire life caused a singularity to bloom.
HUUM!
This singularity was unique. This singularity was colorless, like concentrated Quintessence itself. And it bloomed at the very center of his brain, nestled in the space between thought and being.

It felt extremely delicate and intricate as he examined it with his inner senses. Any single thing that could possibly go wrong would cause everything to collapse. The structure was fragile, newly born, struggling to maintain coherence.
And yet, Noah felt unfathomable amounts of effort and Civilizational Authority of Mana and Hunger flow into it like rivers feeding an ocean. And the moment that it was fully formed...
He couldn’t help but gasp as sensation overwhelmed analysis for a brief moment.

This point of colorless brilliance began to feel like a fundamental part of his existence, as natural as his heartbeat or the flow of Primus Mana through his channels. And at this moment, he observed something remarkable.
The crimson-gold flames that were burning him and permeating across his existence could not find their entry into this colorless brilliance.
It became the only part of his existence that was not affected by the curse fromTHE Living Elemental.

And the moment it emerged, a sensation of coolness erupted from it like a wave washing across a shore. It spread across his existence with gentle but persistent force, and it made the excruciating pain... slightly less excruciating.
Slightly more bearable.
It was not relief, not truly, but it was the difference between drowning and keeping one’s head above water.
As Noah felt this sensation and catalogued it with careful precision, new prompts bloomed before his vision.
|THE Organ of Civilizationis forming.|
|There are countless ways to attainTHEdistinction, countless paths to enterThe Civilizational Scale of Existence.|

|As of this moment, you are embarking on your own novel way as your Primus Mana has paved the path alongside immense effort and harvest to bring something new into what is considered Observable Existence.|
|THE Organ of Civilizationhas bloomed within your existence.|
|Classification: It can be considered akin to a stairway towardsTHE, towardsThe Civilizational Scale of Existence.|
|Warning: It is novel and unproven. Its development will be guided by you in how it forms and evolves.|
|It sits at a core component of your existence. Any mistakes in its cultivation would mean the immediate collapse of your existence.|
|Current Effect:With THE Organ of Civilization forming, you have gained 1% THE Civilizational Authority Resistance.|
|THE Immolation Of The Sacrilegious Savagecan now be withstood with slightly less excruciating pain, but the pain still persists at a high intensity.|
|THE Organ of Civilizationis inherently connected with yourPrimordial Civilization of Mana and Hunger.|
|It will advance and form its identity as your Civilization progresses.|
|Resource Requirement: Analysis indicates it will need an immense amount of resources and harvest for any advancement, scaled to the quality of infinity inherent in your Primus Mana.|
1% THE Civilizational Authority Resistance.
This was the cooling sensation he felt in a sea of excruciating pain that still occurred, but now the difference was measurable. Quantifiable.

Noah raised his hand with deliberate slowness, testing the change. Gloriously, it did not tremble from the pain as he stood on the surface of the Cultivation Citadel. His entire existence was still being burned by crimson-gold flames, but at this moment...he did not tremble.

His eyes flashed with a sense of solemnity as he looked inward, examining the space in his brain whereTHE Organ of Civilizationlay. He could barely perceive its circular shape and the colorless brilliance that reminded him of pure Quintessence.
But it felt like an endless black hole that would take everything he could feed it, and its results... would be unfathomably immense.
WhenTHE Living Elementalcursed his existence with such malice and certainty, never could he have possibly dreamed that Noah would somehow gain this as a byproduct, could he?
The irony was not lost on Noah. The curse had forced him to evolve. The pain had created the path forward.

And now that it did bloom, now that he saw a light at the end of a horrendously dark tunnel, he would barrel towards this light with relentless speed until one day he would makeTHE Living Elementalfeel like collapsing his own existence.
Because even though he persevered, even though what he felt right now was still excruciating but slightly more bearable, his existence had still risen up with the thought multiple times of surrender.
Maybe if I collapsed myself, I could escape this pain.
That thought had risen multiple times like a demon whispering in his ear, and he had crushed it down every time. Only by will, and will alone.
He hated that any existence could cause him to feel such a sensation. He hated that he had been brought so low, forced to consider ending himself just to escape torment.
He would rectify this. He would pay this forward with interest compounded over eons.
THE Living Elementalcould count on it.

Noah stood straighter on the Cultivation Citadel, his body still wreathed in flames but no longer trembling. He observed the weight of existence pressing down on him from this place, noted how it interacted with the curse and his newly formed Organ.
Everything was data. Everything was a variable to be measured and understood.
And understanding, he had learned, was the first step to victory.
Knowledge continued to be key.
He looked up towards where The Infiniverse hovered above, watching him with those eyes of golden light.

chapters.title: Chapter 4501: Dawn II
paragraphs: As Noah was thinking all of this, The Infiniverse approached with a solemn expression etched across her features.
"Slightly less excruciating?" she asked quietly. "Bearable?"

Noah looked at her and felt a sense of warmth pierce through the constant burning. He knew what she had done. He knew how she had exposed herself to his pain through their connection, how she should know exactly what he now felt every moment of his existence.
So he simply nodded as he said with calm certainty, "Less excruciating."
The Infiniverse nodded in acknowledgment as she calmly said, "Okay. There is lots of work to be done."

Noah looked at her and nodded before he spoke with deliberate care. "Take it easy on the countless lifeforms out there.THE Living Elementalis responsible for this. The weak Living Elementals and Fold Dwellers across the Folds are not. Let’s make sure our rage does not spill onto them unnecessarily."
At his words, The Infiniverse paused as she calmly said, "They won’t feel my rage, but...there will be conquest."
BOOM!
The air trembled with the weight of her declaration.

"I’ve never needed to conquer to grow in a while now," The Infiniverse continued with terrifying calm. "I don’t need to devour the Folds. I don’t need to conquer the countless lifeforms in Observable Existence to advance my power. But I have a duty.You are my duty. And I plan to fulfill my duty, no matter what. No matter if all of Observable Existence has to burn for this duty to be completed."
With such terrifying words carrying the weight of absolute conviction, The Infiniverse disappeared from the space.

Noah looked at where she had been standing as he shook his head and continued to try and understandTHE Organ of Civilizationthat had just bloomed within him. He sent his Primus Mana and Civilizational Authority of Mana and Hunger into it with careful precision, observing the reaction.
The organ responded to his probing with something like hunger.

He came to find that the more he flooded his Primus Mana and Civilizational Authority of Mana and Hunger into it,THE Organ of Civilizationactually pulsed with eagerness like a genuine organ demanding sustenance. The sensation was strange and new, as if a heart had appeared in his brain that beat to a different rhythm than the rest of his body.
So he flooded more and more into it with methodical persistence.

After a few minutes of continuous feeding, droves of Primus Mana and Civilizational Authority of Mana and Hunger flowing into it like rivers into an ocean, he finally received a reaction from this thing that bore the distinction ofTHE.
THE Organ of Civilizationpulsed with brilliant blue gold light.

Noah felt in the next moment, centered in his head, an unfathomably dense and pure authority being released from this organ. It caused all of his existence to buzz with resonance, every cell vibrating in harmony with this new frequency.
New prompts bloomed before his vision.
|THE Organ of Civilizationhas processed the provided resources.|
|Result: An extremely unique andUnquantifiable Unit of Everythinghas appeared within your existence.|
|Effect: Just from the appearance of thisUnquantifiable Unit of Everything, the Complexity and Purity of your existence has doubled from 3.5 Septillion to 7 Septillion.|
|This unit defies standard measurement and categorization.|
|Unknown potential applications detected.|
The prompts were ridiculous to see as Noah’s eyes pulsed with tyranny and immensity, but he forced himself to analyze them logically.
First, yes, his Complexity and Purity had risen ridiculously due to the excruciating pain he was always bearing sinceTHE Living ElementalappliedTHE Immolation Of The Sacrilegious Savage.
He had continued to gain more than one hundred Sextillion every little while until at this point it had reached 3.5 Septillion before this sudden doubling.

The rate of increase was utterly ridiculous when one truly thought about it with any degree of objectivity. The jump to Sextillion had been grand initially, with Khor having been in the lead with just a little bit over 200 Sextillion. Of course The Infiniverse had taken the lead when she reached 1 Septillion through her own growth.
And due to the excruciating pain from this curse, Noah had exploded upwards to 3.5 Septillion and now to 7 Septillion with this single production.

Whenever he observed this number jumping rapidly as he continued to advance more and more in Complexity and Purity, and yet absolutely nothing had occurred to diminish the terrifying pain of thr curse within his existence, it further confirmed the truth he had been analyzing.
In the future, when it came to dealing with existences that had the power ofTHE, Complexity and Purity would not be metrics that held immense importance.
An unfathomable qualitative leap would be occurring as the power of the existences of theCivilizational Scalewas still a little hard to grasp fully.

Because of this reality, something that came from within his existence from an organ that had the label ofTHE, something that emerged from such a thing...could effectively double his Complexity and Purity so simply.
Noah looked within his existence with careful observation to examine theUnquantifiable Unit of Everythingthat flowed out ofTHE Organ of Civilization.
It was remarkable to behold.

The unit appeared as a Mobius strip suspended in conceptual space, and when he focused his perception inside of it, he observed an extremely dense and pure concentration of Primus Mana and Civilizational Authority of Mana and Hunger.

These authorities were spinning around each other in complex patterns akin to how an atom had electrons, protons, and neutrons moving in orbital shells. The Primus Mana formed the core nucleus, dense and brilliant blue-gold. Around it, the Civilizational Authority of Mana orbited in one shell, while the Civilizational Authority of Hunger orbited in another, both moving in synchronized patterns that defied simple physics.
The whole structure twisted through the Mobius strip configuration, meaning the inside became the outside and the outside became the inside in an endless loop of impossible wonder.

Noah studied it with analytical marvel as he felt this extremely dense type of authority remain floating in his head nearTHE Organ of Civilization.As he tried his best to quantify and understand it through examination and logical deduction, more information bloomed.
|Unquantifiable Unit of Everything|
|Classification: An authority of mysterious origins originating fromTHE Organ of Civilization.|
|Effect: Its mere appearance within your existence has effectively doubled the Complexity and Purity of your existence.|
|Potential Applications: Could potentially be utilized in reinforcing your body, activating an ability or feature, fueling a Principle, or other unknown functions.|
|Results are entirely unknown on exactly what could occur upon utilization.|
|Current Quantity: 1 Unit|
|Stability: Ridiculously Stable|
|Recommendation: Experimentation advised with caution.|

Noah wanted to marvel at the wonders that he was witnessing, to study this new discovery with the thoroughness it deserved, but the excruciating pain of the continued burning ofTHE Immolation Of The Sacrilegious Savagecaused him to wake from his analytical reverie.
He breathed out slowly, feeling the flames still consuming him.

An excruciating pain was still ever present in his existence even when he was discovering marvels and wonders this pain indirectly led to. The irony was not lost on him that his greatest torment had birthed one his greatest opportunity.
At this moment, he looked inward atTHE Organ of Civilizationand began continuously flooding it with Primus Mana and Civilizational Authority of Mana and Hunger with renewed purpose.
If one Unit could double his Complexity and Purity, what could ten do? What could a hundred do?
At the same time, he pondered the question that demanded experimentation.
How should he test out what wonders theUnquantifiable Unit of Everythingheld? And what exactly more didTHE Organ of Civilizationhold in store as it developed?
The logical approach would be controlled testing, but the curse burning through him suggested that time might be a luxury he couldn’t afford to waste on excessive caution.
Noah observed the Mobius strip of concentrated authority floating in his consciousness and made a decision.
He would feedTHE Organ of Civilizationcontinuously and accumulate more Units. Once he had several, he could afford to experiment with one while keeping the others in reserve.
The pain continued to burn, but now it had a purpose beyond simply being endured.
It was fuel for evolution and the price of ascension.
And Noah would pay it gladly if it meant gaining the power to makeTHE Living Elementalregret the day he had decided to curse him.
The Cultivation Citadel pressed down on him with its weight, and Noah stood firm beneath it, no longer trembling.
His hand reached up to touch his temple whereTHE Organ of Civilizationpulsed with hunger, and he smiled despite the burning.
"Let’s see what you can truly do," he whispered to the organ, and flooded it with even more authority!
HUUM!
The organ pulsed in response, already beginning to process the new resources.
And Noah waited with analytical patience to see what would emerge next.

chapters.title: Chapter 4502: Dawn III
paragraphs: Karma.

The concept has been debated across countless civilizations and cultures throughout the ages. Some believe it to be an immutable law of reality, a cosmic balance sheet where every action is recorded and every debt eventually comes due. They argue that Existence itself keeps score, that righteousness will be rewarded and wickedness punished in time.
Others believe it to be nothing more than false hope, a comforting story told to the oppressed to help them sleep at night while their suffering continues unabated.

And when one observed reality with cold objectivity, the second perspective seemed to hold more weight. More often than not, the vile tyrant crushing entire populations under his boot would die peacefully in his bed surrounded by luxury.

The rich noble oppressing the masses would pass his wealth to his children and never face consequences. The corrupt entity wielding power without responsibility would ascend higher and higher, their crimes buried beneath mountains of success.
Karma, it seemed, rarely made house calls.
But the few times that karma did visit such beings, when the scales finally balanced and the debt came due...
Karma could be a bitch.
On the other side of The Veil.
In The Lands of The Dead.
Past the vast swathes of regions and Citadels of The Dead that the Great Usurper was silently spreading his grand Derivative Civilization of Idle Existence through.

In the deepest reaches of The Lands of Dead, there existed a domain that very few Guiders of Order were even allowed to approach. It existed in layers of existence far above everything else, in an isolated space removed from the normal flow of reality.
Inside of it, all that could be seen was the white brilliance of Order and the obsidian brilliance of Death mixing together in patterns of terrible beauty.
At this moment, livid words echoed out inside this isolated region with the force of thunder.
"A vile sycophantic fuck and the Young Order he defiles... he actually dares to do this shit?!"
The roaring voice belonged to none other thanTHE Dead Order, and she was not having a good day.

She sat upon a brilliant massive white marbled throne that gleamed with concentrated authority. Her lower body was entirely covered in burning crimson-gold flames that climbed higher with each passing moment. Her upper body surged with seas of white Order that crashed down continuously to push these flames from spreading any further up her form.
Her gaze was currently one of complete lividity and rage, and there were several things contributing to her fury.

One was the simple fact that if she had not been maddeningly laughing at the misfortune of Osmont and how he would soon perish from the curse, she would not have been caught off guard by the reality of him crossing The Veil in that space between spaces.
With her power fully focused, she would have been able to grab hold of him in an instant and crushed him for his audacity.

But due to her carelessness, her arrogant assumption that he was already defeated, she had only discovered him when he was already in contact with her leg. And after that moment of contact, her first course of action had been to prevent the spread of the flames across her entire being rather than pursue him.
In that brief instant of divided attention, she had allowed him to escape back across The Veil.
She was fuming at this moment, her existence trembling with rage. A lesser being had effectively played their hand against her and won, all because of her carelessness and overconfidence.
The karma that followed was truly a bitch.
And the price to pay was ridiculously heavy.
The pain of the curse ofTHE Living Elementalwas horrendously excruciating even for her.THE Dead Orderheld the distinction ofTHEin capital letters, but this was only partly true in her current state.
She was not the complete Order. She was Dead.

Any existence who could not maintain their Primordial Civilization and was actually collapsed, who had experienced the cessation of their grand power, effectively lost the full distinction ofTHEfor a period of time until they emerged strong enough to reclaim it in the future.
THE Dead Orderhad not fully reclaimed her power yet. She could only be considered halfway recovered from her collapse, struggling to rebuild what had been lost.
She was far grander than a FalseTHE, but she was still not a fullTHEentity with complete power.

So while facingTHE Immolation Of The Sacrilegious Savage, even though she resisted the excruciating pain that other entities would be feeling with this curse through sheer force of her partial authority, she still felt at least half of the intended pain.

The ass ofTHE Dead Orderwas being whooped right now by the curse of THE Living Elemental, both figuratively and literally as her lower half was actually burning with flames that refused to be fully extinguished.

And she could either endure this excruciating burning for the foreseeable future while dedicating the rest of her power to ensure that it did not spread to all of her existence and consume her completely...
Or...
Her expression twisted in utter anger and apathy at the same time, the two emotions warring across her features. She raised her head upward with indecision visible in her ancient eyes.
The burning sensation down below pulsed with fresh intensity, and that pain resolved her indecision instantly.
She gazed up decisively towards the space above her throne.

"You promised me three times that you would act on my behalf," she said with cold clarity. "Three times. These flames burning across my existence would derail everything that I have planned as I would be forced to focus on them constantly. I do not wish for that."

"At this time, get rid of these flames for me. And remove the capability of them to ever affect me again."

She wanted to be absolutely thorough with her words, leaving no room for misinterpretation. Her utilizing this solution was a heavy choice, a debt she was calling in that she would remember Osmont for forcing her to spend.

Her gaze remained decisive and unwavering.

Existence in the surroundings twisted in ways that should not have been possible. It felt like all of the surrounding space dipped and folded to cover the body ofTHE Dead Orderlike a veil descending from above.
A terrifying flash ofTHE Civilizational Authority of Existencewas exerted, raw and absolute.

More than that, she could feel that such similar flames or type of curse would not be harmful to her in the future, as if she had been granted immunity. So Osmont would never be able to spread it to her again!
Only THE Civilizational Authority can go against THE Civilizational Authority.
This proved to be true at this very moment in the starkest possible terms.

THE Dead Orderhad paid a heavy cost, spent one of her three promised interventions, in order to get past a problem that another being was giving every single ounce of their existence to solve and endure.
And yet a few words from her and moments later it was resolved completely.
The disparity was absolute. The difference in scale was undeniable.
Her eyes flashed with lividity as she looked outward as if she could see past the far distant Veil that separated her domain from Observable Existence.
"Osmont," she said with venom dripping from each syllable. "Osmont. Osmont!"
The grandeur of Order and Death began to permeate all around her throne as her words echoed out with pure malice.

"Since you are so good at pissing off THE Entities, I will add myself to the list with pleasure," she continued with cold fury. "You think yourself safe on the other side of The Veil, just because I cannot cross it? Because you hide behind that barrier like a coward?"
She leaned forward on her throne, her presence intensifying.

"Okay. It is time for you to learn a lesson. You’re going to learn that even if I do not have the full distinction of THE, I am still half of such a being. And half is more than enough to deal with an insect like you."
Her voice rose to a roar.
"You’re going to learn. You are going to fucking learn!"
As she roared with such hatred and vitriol, the surrounding existence seemed to respond to her fury.
The space around her throne grew just a little dimmer. Just a little less vibrant.
As if reality itself was holding its breath in anticipation of whatTHE Dead Orderwould do next.
And in that moment of terrible promise, karma prepared to make another house call.
This time, the target was named Noah Osmont.
Whether he would ever be reached though, was unknown!

The concept has been debated across countless civilizations and cultures throughout the ages.
Some believe it to be an immutable law of reality, a cosmic balance sheet where every action is recorded and every debt eventually comes due.
They argue that Existence itself keeps score, that righteousness will be rewarded and wickedness punished in time.
Others believe it to be nothing more than false hope, a comforting story told to the oppressed to help them sleep at night while their suffering continues unabated.
And when one observed reality with cold objectivity, the second perspective seemed to hold more weight.
More often than not, the vile tyrant crushing entire populations under his boot would die peacefully in his bed surrounded by luxury.
The rich noble oppressing the masses would pass his wealth to his children and never face consequences.
The corrupt entity wielding power without responsibility would ascend higher and higher, their crimes buried beneath mountains of success.
Karma, it seemed, rarely made house calls.
But the few times that karma did visit such beings, when the scales finally balanced and the debt came due...
Karma could be a bitch.

In The Lands of The Dead.

It existed in layers of existence far above everything else, in an isolated space removed from the normal flow of reality.

chapters.title: Chapter 4503: Dawn IV
paragraphs: InsideTHE Loom.
In a domain bathed by the grandeur ofTHE Primordial Civilization of Paradox.
WHOOSH!

The doors of a capsule hissed open with precision, releasing pressurized air in a controlled burst. The capsule itself was a marvel of advanced construction, shining with golden light that pulsed in rhythmic patterns. Its surface was smooth and seamless, composed of materials that seemed to exist between states of paradoxical matter.
From this glorious apparatus, the figure of Ambessa emerged.

Her entire existence looked utterly changed from before. Her hair now flowed like rivers of liquid gold, each strand catching light and reflecting it in impossible angles. Her eyes pulsed with an intense crimson-gold light.
Her entire existence was scintillating and shining, as if she had become a forged treasure that could only be found in the earliest, most primordial Folds of existence.
From a distance, the figure of Forge Emperor Niso approached with measured steps and looked at her with pride mixed with caution.
"How do you feel?" he asked. "You have gotten the honor of Specialization that even I have not received yet. At this moment in time, our roles could be considered completely changed."
Ambessa looked at her mentor and smiled warmly despite the overwhelming sensations coursing through her.
"Don’t worry, old man. I still see you as my mentor regardless of how far I go," she said with genuine affection. "As for how I feel... well, this is just ridiculous."

She reached out and felt for her power with careful attention, observing the changes that had occurred. She could feel that her current Complexity and Purity had spilled past 1,000 Sextillion, or was sitting at approximately 1 Septillion.
But she was not even amazed at the sheer number of Complexity and Purity, which would have been staggering before. Instead, her attention was drawn elsewhere.
"My Complexity and Purity is currently high," she said slowly, searching for words. "But..."
She almost could not explain the sensation properly, as if words were insufficient for what she was experiencing.

In front of her, Forge Master Niso smiled with understanding and said, "You are now anUncertainty Paradox. You carry with you the building blocks toThe False THE. Complexity and Purity will matter less and less as you head towards anything that has the distinction ofTHE."
He gestured to her transformed body.

"The biggest thing for you to receive from this Specialization should beTHE False Uncertainty Paradoxical Spine, packed with the complete automatic utilization of 9 Principles relating to Paradox. Get familiar with it as afterwards, they will have you meet with the other leaders on exactly how things would be unfolding for the missions outside ofTHE Loom."
Forge Master Niso had just finished saying this when in the next moment...
HUUM!

Blazing auras could instantly be felt approaching from the distance. The sleek laboratory-like white-gold domain they were in had its doors opened in the far distance, and the auras of utterly terrifying entities began to pour in like a tide.
Shockingly, Axiom Architect Surion, who held a terrifying amount of power and authority, was actually moving in the back as multiple others were leading in front of him.

Ambessa and Forge Master Niso were astonished by this reversal of expected hierarchy. They recognized some of the faces of the entities that were walking in, distinguished figures within theShelters of THE Loom.
One of them was an entity that Axiom Architect Surion had mentioned before, when they were initially deployed as avatars outside ofTHE Loom. They were looking atParadox Anax Belial!
An entity with the designation ofThe False THE!
And shockingly, beside him were two other entities who carried the same terrifying designation.

One was a woman with an extremely icy gaze, her entire body surrounded by frost that made the air crystallize around her. Even with her recent transformation and elevation, Ambessa felt like this woman, this Early Creature, could crush her with her gaze alone.
Ambessa searched her memory rapidly, matching the face to information she had been given. This should beElemental Anax Poana!

The other FalseTHEhere was wreathed in purple storms as lightning and thunder boomed around his muscular body in continuous displays. His bronze skin looked like polished metal, and his frame was built like a celestial statue carved by master artisans. Currently his gaze was also cold and focused, but thisElemental Anax,Ambessa did not recognize from any briefings.
She only managed these brief glances before Axiom Architect Surion introduced the three FalseTHEto them with a sense of calmness and deep respect.

"Ambessa, Forge Master Niso, allow me to introduceParadox Anax Belial, Elemental Anax Poana, and Elemental Anax Theron,"Surion said formally. "They have come with urgent directives regarding operations outsideTHE Loom."

Ambessa inclined her head respectfully, trying to read the situation. After a moment of tense silence, she cautiously asked with careful words, "To what do we owe the pleasure of having the presence of such distinguished beings here? Surely the issue of the forces outside ofTHE Loomhas not progressed to warrant your personal attention and intervention?"
At these words, she felt the expressions of the Elemental Anax pulse with something dangerous. She quieted down immediately, sensing she had touched on something volatile.
What the hell had happened with the Living Elementals to make them act like this?
As she was processing this development,Elemental Anax Poanastepped forward with measured grace. Her voice was cold and absolute when she spoke.

"The entity known as Noah Osmont, the creature who collapsed your avatar outside ofTHE Loom, has been labeled ASacrilegious Savageunder the customs ofTHE Primordial Civilization of Elementals," she said with formal weight. "His actions and insults to our Civilization are unforgivable, with his existence deemed forabsolute collapse before the emergence of The Glorious Evolution."
She looked directly at Ambessa.
"Every single one of you that is capable of descending outside ofTHE Loomwill be working directly with me or others to ensure the absolute collapse of this being. Is that understood?"
Ambessa was astonished at the seriousness and solemnity of it all. Her analytical mind raced with questions.
"What did he do in such a short period of time to insult The Primordial Civilization of Elementals like this?" she asked carefully.
Her question was faced with immediate coldness. Poana’s gaze hardened.
"You are a soldier. Soldiers do not question orders.Do you understand?"

The atmosphere grew heavy and oppressive. Ambessa frowned at being shut down so completely, and she felt the hand of Forge Emperor Niso on her shoulder, a gentle pressure that told her not to erupt or push further.
She simply nodded and replied through gritted teeth, "I understand."
Elemental Anax Poananodded with satisfaction and said, "Good. We will begin by having you accept a portion of my power and consciousness into your existence."
Ambessa’s gaze changed dramatically at this declaration. This was something that she did not want, something that went against everything she had been building.

Her entire existence burned with Paradox as her foundation. If another foreign power permeated across her existence, especially one from a different Primordial Civilization, it would taint her Way permanently.
Could they not find another method? Why not haveParadox Anax Belialdo this? Why were they all acting with such extreme measures?
She wanted to ask these questions and she wanted to have a proper dialogue about alternatives. But she felt the hand of her mentor squeeze her shoulder again with warning pressure.
She only grit her teeth harder and said, "Understood."
At her agreement,Elemental Anax Poanagestured for Ambessa to sit in a prepared position. Ambessa complied, settling into a meditative posture.

Poana sat across from her with fluid grace, and her body began to erupt with a terrifying icyTHE False Civilizational Authority of Elemental.The temperature in the room dropped dramatically as frost began to form on every surface.
She raised her hand slowly and deliberately, then tapped it against Ambessa’s forehead.
A terrifying power began to flow into Ambessa’s existence like a flood breaking through a dam!
As Poana maintained the transfer, she turned her head towards Paradox Anax Belial without breaking concentration.
"Brother Belial, I will leave it to you to get all the others ready as well," she said with calm authority.
Belial, the terrifying being surrounded by swirling Paradox authority, smiled with an eerie expression that didn’t quite reach his eyes.

"Of course, Sister Poana," he said smoothly. "The weavings of Paradox are here to help all other Civilizations withinTHE Loom. We will rectify the wrong that has been committed and ensure that the Sacrilegious Savage attains their proper end."
With such words hanging in the air, Ambessa watched through increasingly blurred vision as her existence buzzed with conflicting authorities.
Belial hummed a tune without words as he left the domain with smooth steps.
Her gaze flashed coldly as she felt even more power ofTHE False Civilizational Authority of Elementalflowing into her existence in continuous waves!
She could feel it spreading through her pathways, integrating with her being in ways that would be permanent and irreversible!
Terrifying and profound changes were occurring in this small subsection ofTHE Loom.

And elsewhere, in a domain of absolute Elemental authority, a terrifying force felt the establishment of their curse through vast distances.THE Living Elementalobserved something that should not have been possible.
The entity the curse was attached to, the lesser pathetic entity that should have collapsed within seconds, had actually not collapsed this whole time.
So this terrifying force, this being with a completeTHEdistinction, prepared another response in case the Sacrilegious Savage continued to persevere and did not collapse their existence as intended.
Resources were being mobilized. Agents were being prepared. Plans were being set into motion.
It was a moment where a spark had been lit in the darkness.
And a glorious fire was about to rage across Observable Existence!

chapters.title: Chapter 4504: The Infinite Unfurling! I
paragraphs: In the Cultivation Citadel.
Noah sat on the ground with his legs crossed in a meditative posture as crimson-gold flames continued to burn all around him in their endless dance of torment.
Even while withstanding such excruciating pain that would have long since collapsed lesser beings, his expression remained calm and analytical. His eyes were even showing an expectant light.

The reason was none other than the fact that at this moment, after almost an hour of continuous feeding of resources intoTHE Organ of Civilization, he had managed to form nineUnquantifiable Units of Everything.
Nine Mobius strip objects floated in his head at this moment, each one a masterwork of impossible geometry and concentrated authority!
And his entire existence buzzed with immensity for it.

After the ninth one formed, no more appeared even after he poured in seas of Primus Mana and Civilizational Authority of Mana and Hunger for double the amount of time. The Organ simply absorbed the resources without producing anything new.
So it seemed that nine was the maximum capacity at this time.
Nine could be considered a low number, depending on what terrifying usage theseUnquantifiable Units of Everythingactually held when applied to problems.
And Noah considered them terrifying from the moment the second one had proceeded to double his 7 Septillion Complexity and Purity, bringing it up to 14 Septillion just from its appearance!

Sadly, the doubling effect did not continue thereafter. With the third appearance and every other appearance of theUnquantifiable Unit of Everythingup until the ninth one, his Complexity and Purity only increased by seven Septillion each.
After the ninthUnquantifiable Unit of Everything, his total stood at 63 Septillion Complexity and Purity.
The jump was staggering. From 3.5 Septillion to 63 Septillion in the span of an hour!

Seeing the ridiculous effects that they had just from being formed and remaining inside his existence passively, his expectations were immensely high for what they could produce when actively utilized.
At this moment, he gave a simple command.
"Come out."
HUUM!

The firstUnquantifiable Unit of Everythingfloated out of his existence with graceful motion. It caused the surrounding air to shimmer as if reality itself was bending around its presence. The atmospheric authority in the surroundings instantly began buzzing and increasing in concentration by at least tenfold!
The Cultivation Citadel responded to its presence, the weight of existence pressing down even harder as if acknowledging something of profound importance.
When it came to how he wanted to test it, the description had stated that it could be applicable to countless things.
But for now, he would start with something he understood well.
"Use theUnquantifiable Unit of Everythingas the authority to activate Perpetual Harvest’s Harvest Festival Endowment on The Infiniverse."
A simple command.
Yet the moment that Noah gave such a directive, theUnquantifiable Unit of Everythingbegan to spin with silent glow and intensity.
And then it warped out of existence in the next moment.
Just disappeared completely from his perception!
And a moment later...
BOOM!
Noah’s vision became covered by verdant-green seas of brilliance that erupted from nowhere and everywhere at once!
The prompts that bloomed were unlike anything he had seen before.
|The Unquantifiable Unit of Everythingdisdains its immensity being used for such a simple task.|
|Note: Its breadth is capable of empowering your entire Civilization.|
|Perpetual Harvest has been fully activated with theUnquantifiable Unit of Everythingstemming fromTHE Organ of Civilizationas the catalyzing authority.|
|The Infiniverse has gained an endowment of 5,000 Sextillion Complexity and Purity (5 Septillion).|
|The strongest amongst your budding Civilization have also been empowered by 500 Sextillion Complexity and Purity each.|
|Recipients include: The 54 Million+ Primus Inevitabilities, all those who have visited the Early Veiled Shore, and those who share a significant enough connection with your existence.|
|Introductory access to The Seed of the Grand Principle of Mana Genesis has been granted to all recipients mentioned above.|
|The Infiniverse has gained the capability to form The Primordial Primus Mana Folds of Existence.|
|Effect: The Infiniverse can now create self-sustaining Folds of reality that generate Primus Mana perpetually, serving as resource nodes for your Civilization.|
|Current Formation Limit: 10 Primordial Primus Mana Folds of Existence.|
|The Infiniverse has gained the architectural blueprint for The Eternal Forge of Existential Advancement.|

|Effect: A grand structure that can be built to continuously forge equipment, treasures, and existential enhancements for all members of your Civilization. Items produced will scale and continue to scale with the Civilization’s overall power.|
|Construction Requirements: Available resources sufficient. Construction can begin immediately.|
After Noah read over the prompts and felt the terrifying waves of changes brought about by the usage of a single Unquantifiable Unit of Everything, he was genuinely astonished.
His eyes flashed with immense brilliance as he analyzed the boons given with careful attention.
The primary empowerment alone was unfathomable. The Infiniverse gaining 5 Septillion that easily was ridiculous.
But the secondary effects were what truly caught his mind.

The Seed of the Grand Principle of Mana Genesis meant that his entire inner circle, millions of Primus Inevitabilities, would soon be cultivating and nurturing a Principle. How hard was it to gain access to a Principle?
And yet now...oh!
More than this, +500 Sextillion Complexity and Purity to all the Primus Inevitabilities and others!
Oh!
The Primordial Primus Mana Folds of Existencewas another ridiculous boon to rise.
AndThe Eternal Forge of Existential Advancement...ah! Equipment and treasures that scaled with Civilization power meant that as his people grew stronger, their tools would grow with them.
All of this from asingleUnquantifiable Unit of Everything.
He still had eight more.
In the distance, he felt The Infiniverse’s presence surge with newfound power. Through their connection, he could feel her wonder.
But again, Complexity and Purity was grand, but it did not mean everything!
Noah looked inward at the remaining eightUnquantifiable Units of Everythingfloating in his consciousness and asked himself the only question that mattered.
Just how terrifying was this Unquantifiable Unit of Everything stemming fromTHE Organ of Civilization?
He had to remind himself thatTHE Organ of Civilizationbloomed as something completely new in Observable Existence.
It meant that even in The Earliest Folds,THE Creatureand all others with the distinction ofTHEdid not have this as part of their pathway towards such power, or as a component of their current selves!
This was novel and unique to him.
This was his own path being forged, and it was proving to be more terrifying than he had dared to dream.
The crimson-gold flames still burned across his existence, but now they felt different somehow. Not less painful, but more purposeful.

They had forced him to evolve. To undergo a Glorious Evolution. They had pushed him to discover this Organ. They had inadvertently given him a weapon that he really wanted to use to cut down THE Living Elemental!
Noah allowed himself a small smile despite the pain.
"Let’s see what the rest of you can do," he murmured, looking at the eight remaining Units!
